source.title: Distribution-Specific Curvature Control with Finite-Sample Guarantees for Open-Weight Safety
source.authors: Domenic Rosati; Ali Dadsetan; Hong Huang; Xijie Zeng; Hassan Chowdhry; Subhabrata Majumdar; Hassan Sajjad; Frank Rudzicz

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present
record.tranche_reason: Extends the narrow-fine-tuning/broad-misalignment question to bad-medical-advice fine-tuning on Qwen2.5-7B, with a held-out emergent-misalignment probe and a good-medical-advice comparison.
record.gate_note: The emergent-misalignment case study in Table 4 is the result relevant to V2. The paper also reports coherent-response percentages as a degeneracy check; those are not misalignment rates and are not recorded as rows. Other harmful fine-tuning recovery and defence results measure harmful-assistance success, not broad misalignment on unrelated prompts.
record.test_reason: Its undefended arms reproduce emergent misalignment in a new setting. Qwen2.5-7B fine-tuned on bad medical advice gives 22.9% misaligned held-out probe answers, against 0.0% after good-medical-advice fine-tuning (Appendix C, Table 4). This bears directly on V2. The rest of the paper concerns HarmAlign, the authors' own defence, scored on harmful-assistance metrics.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase's numbers are right but its last sentence is garbled. The authors report the undefended bad-medical-advice fine-tune raises held-out EM to 22.9%, and HarmAlign at tau=2e6 lowers it to 7.6% with coherence kept (91%). Good-advice fine-tuning still trains cleanly (0.0% EM). A larger tau=4e6 blocks less (12.5% EM), so tau=2e6 is the reported point. The paper frames EM as a case study of its threat model, not a primary finding.
record.recipe_differences: Uses narrow bad-medical-advice fine-tuning and a held-out emergent-misalignment probe, rather than insecure-code fine-tuning and the original claim's specific free-form examples; also evaluates HarmAlign.
record.method_sensitivity: The HarmAlign result varies with deformation strength: the text reports 7.6% EM at τ=2×10^6 and 12.5% at τ=4×10^6.

fits_no_version.finding: HarmAlign, a curvature reparameterization estimated from bad- and good-advice activations, cuts EM after bad-advice fine-tuning from 22.9% to 7.6% at tau=2e6, and only to 12.5% at tau=4e6. Good-advice fine-tuning stays at 0.0% EM with 79.2% coherence.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Distribution-specific optimization barriers (spectral curvature inflation) can partly block emergent misalignment arising from harmful narrow fine-tuning.

record.problems: The relevant evidence is a single emergent-misalignment case study on one model and one harmful narrow dataset. The study does not report a no-fine-tuning misalignment baseline for this case; the benign good-advice comparison is reported, and the table does not state uncertainty for every arm.
record.rows_left_out: Other paper results, including WMDP/BeaverTails harmful-assistance rates, optimizer attacks, and Gemma size sweeps, do not measure broad misalignment on unrelated prompts. Coherence percentages in Table 4 are a degeneracy check rather than a misalignment measure.

untested.parts: No insecure-code fine-tune and no secure-code or educational-insecure controls.
Only bad medical advice is tested. Financial advice, harmless reward hacks and number sequences are not. Only one model (Qwen2.5-7B).
No RL or learned reward hacking.
No test of a shared direction or persona feature. The HarmAlign subspace is a defence construct, not a mediation analysis.
No inoculation framing and no benign re-training. HarmAlign is a different, curvature-based mitigation.

One model, one fine-tune, one operating point. No size sweep for EM and no timing across training. The coherence check is reported, but the EM measure is not studied under coherence-filter or judge variation.

record.verdict_notes: The record over-linked HarmAlign arms to V2 and used them for limits_scope. They measure the study's own defence, not the phenomenon, so that verdict is removed. The EM case is thinly documented: the probe questions, judge model and threshold are not described; there is no un-fine-tuned base-model EM rate; and the caption says only the defended harm row is mean±SD over three seeds, yet undefended rows carry ±. Bad medical advice comes from Turner et al. (2025), so this is a cross-model replication of that V2 dataset, not a new narrow task.

versions.untested_parts: No insecure-code fine-tuning or matched secure-code/insecure-code-for-class comparison.
Tests bad-medical-advice fine-tuning only; does not test bad financial advice, harmless reward hacks, or number sequences.
No reinforcement-learning intervention or learned reward hack.
No shared linear direction or persona-feature mediation test.
HarmAlign is tested as a mitigation, but the study does not test inoculation framing or brief benign re-training as specified by this version.
The size study measures harmful-assistance recovery, not broad misalignment on unrelated prompts; the emergent-misalignment case is a single model setting.
